name: Huang Ruohong
current_role: Executive Director and Chairman, Redco Properties Group (HKEX: 1622)
profile: Huang Ruohong (Wong Yeuk Hung, 黄若虹) founded Redco Properties, a Shenzhen-headquartered residential developer listed in Hong Kong, and is its controlling shareholder (about 40%). He has chaired the board since March 2017. The company, like many Chinese developers, has been working through a difficult property market.
interesting_fact: He became Redco's board chairman and an executive director in March 2017 in his capacity as controlling shareholder, after building the developer from its Fujian/Jiangxi roots into an HKEX-listed group.
deep_cut_fact: He holds the Hong Kong title of Justice of the Peace (JP), is a member of a national CPPCC committee and serves as vice chairman of the Hong Kong Federation of Fujian Associations.
notes: Known in HK filings as Wong Yeuk Hung. No published IR email found; check latest HKEX annual report for company secretary / IR contact. Avoid referencing the company's debt situation in outreach.

name: Yang Zhen
current_role: Founder and (per 2024 reports) actual controller of Jiajia Food Group (加加食品, SZSE: 002650); no longer chairman
profile: Yang Zhen (杨振, b. 1962, Ningxiang, Hunan) founded Jiajia soy sauce in 1996 and took it public in 2012 as China's first listed soy-sauce maker, earning the nickname 'soy sauce king'. He later stepped back from management to focus on outside investments; a cousin, Yang Xudong, now chairs the company.
interesting_fact: In 2003 he spent RMB 48m, nearly all of Jiajia's profits from its first seven years, to win CCTV's prime-time 'ad king' slot for two months; revenue hit a record RMB 500m in 2004.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he trained at Yiyang Normal College and worked as a Chinese-language teacher. He is credited with inventing the built-in pull-ring soy-sauce bottle cap, and he founded Jiajia in 1996 after Hunan factories turned down his offer to sell the patent for RMB 500k.
notes: Sensitive. Since 2022, Yang and his holding company have repeatedly been listed as debt defaulters, and Jiajia has been ST-flagged over guarantees he arranged. Approach with care, if at all. No personal or office contact published. Go through the Jiajia Food board secretary listed in SZSE filings.

name: Prateek Agarwal
current_role: Head of Strategic Sourcing and Planning, Macleods Pharmaceuticals; promoter-group shareholder (per 2022 DRHP)
profile: Prateek Agarwal is part of the Bawri/Agarwal family that founded Mumbai-based Macleods Pharmaceuticals, a large privately held generics maker known for affordable TB and HIV drugs. He joined the company in 2012, heads strategic sourcing and planning, and was named as a promoter selling shareholder in Macleods' 2022 IPO draft prospectus.
interesting_fact: Macleods, founded in 1989, became a pioneer in low-cost tuberculosis medicines supplied around the world.
deep_cut_fact: He has a bachelor's degree in pharmacy from the University of Mumbai. He has worked at Macleods since 1 August 2012 and is a pharmacist by training, not only a family shareholder.
notes: Low public profile. Son of Macleods chairman Banwarilal Bawri (Agarwal). Co-founder and MD Rajendra Agarwal reportedly died in Nov 2025. The IR email comes from the 2022 IPO draft; the IPO was not completed, so the address may be inactive.

name: Zhang Chunlin
current_role: Founder and former chairman of SafBon Water Service (Shanghai); listed as CEO of Shanghai Yingsu Environment & Technology
profile: Zhang Chunlin (张春霖) founded Shanghai-based SafBon Water Service, a water-treatment engineering and equipment company listed in Shenzhen, and chaired it from 1999 to October 2021. In 2021 he sold a 9.91% stake (about CNY 340m) to Shandong Gaochuang Construction Investment Group, which took control, and he left the company in 2022.
interesting_fact: He sold a 9.91% SafBon stake to state-backed Shandong Gaochuang Construction Investment for about CNY 340m, completed 21 June 2021, handing control of the water-treatment firm he had built since 1999 to a state-linked investor.
deep_cut_fact: He has an MBA from Antai College of Economics & Management at Shanghai Jiao Tong University.

name: Sharan Pasricha
current_role: Founder & President, Ennismore (Accor joint venture); Founder & CEO, Estelle Community
profile: London-based hotelier (b. 1980, Mumbai). He founded Ennismore in 2011, bought The Hoxton in Shoreditch and Gleneagles, and grew The Hoxton into an international chain. In 2021 Ennismore merged into a joint venture with Accor, which now has 16+ lifestyle brands (Mondrian, SLS, 25hours, Mama Shelter) and 180+ hotels. He also runs Estelle Community (Maison Estelle, Estelle Manor).
interesting_fact: He led the 2015 purchase of Scotland's Gleneagles from Diageo. A dozen-plus renovation projects followed, and operating profits were reported at more than £1m a week in 2018. He was made an MBE in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: While a student at Regent's College he started a London marketing agency, RUSH! Media. Before his MBA he spent three years in New Delhi as turnaround CEO of his uncle's leather-manufacturing business. In 2011 his first move as a hotelier was a bid to buy Soho House with founder Nick Jones.

public_contacts.value: https://ennismore.com/contact/ (choose 'Press'; the form routes to info@ennismore.com)

notes: Most accessible person in this lane. He gives frequent trade-press interviews (Skift, Hospitality Design) and fits an entrepreneurship podcast well. info@ennismore.com appears in the contact form's page source as the address for Press enquiries.

name: Li Yikui
current_role: Founder of Dongbao Industrial Group and Tonghua Dongbao Pharmaceutical (SSE: 600867). His son Li Jiahong has chaired Tonghua Dongbao since March 2024.
profile: Li Yikui (李一奎, b. 1951, Jilin) founded what became Tonghua Dongbao in 1984 from a small Tonghua tonic factory. He took it public in Shanghai in 1994, and it grew into a major Chinese insulin maker within the Dongbao Industrial Group. He served as a deputy to the 8th and 10th National People's Congress. Group leadership has since passed to the next generation.
interesting_fact: He started the business in 1984 as the Tonghua Baishan tonic/pharma factory. It listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 1994 and now sells injectable insulin internationally.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in a poor family in Tonghua, Jilin, and graduated from Peking University's biology department with a degree in microbiology and biochemistry. He worked at a state-owned pharmaceutical plant before founding Dongbao.
notes: Alive status not freshly confirmed (zh.wikipedia listed him as living as of 2021; no death report seen). He has handed day-to-day control to the next generation, so the company route is the only published channel. Web-search budget ran out during this lane, so this entry relied on direct page fetches.

name: Yang Huanming
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, BGI Group (Shenzhen); academician, Chinese Academy of Sciences
profile: Yang Huanming (杨焕明, b. 1952, near Wenzhou) is a geneticist who co-founded the Beijing Genomics Institute (BGI) in 1999 and led China's part of the international Human Genome Project. BGI later moved to Shenzhen and became a commercial genomics group whose listed arm, BGI Genomics, is the basis of his wealth. He is a member of the CAS, the Leopoldina and the US National Academy of Sciences.
interesting_fact: His BGI team's draft sequence of the indica rice genome was the cover story of Science on 5 April 2002, an early sign that China had become a genome-sequencing power.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he was the only Chinese appointee to the international research panel of President Obama's Presidential Commission for the Study of Bioethical Issues, which examined the 1940s Guatemala syphilis experiments. He earned his PhD at the University of Copenhagen's Institute of Medical Genetics.
notes: Scientist-founder who often speaks at conferences (e.g. ICG). A conference keynote may be an easier route than cold email. He is a well-known advocate of open genomic data, a strong podcast angle.

name: Hu Xuemin
current_role: Early shareholder and former director (2014-2020) of Eoptolink Technology (SZSE: 300502); no current board role found
profile: Hu Xuemin (胡学民) sat on the board of Chengdu-based Eoptolink Technology, an optical-transceiver maker founded in 2008 by chairman Gao Guangrong, from December 2014 to December 2020, which covers its 2016 Shenzhen IPO. His wealth comes from his Eoptolink stake. Eoptolink has since become a major supplier of high-speed optical modules for AI data centres.
interesting_fact: Eoptolink, where he was a director, became a big winner of the AI data-centre build-out. It was rated the world's seventh-largest transceiver vendor in 2022, bought US silicon-photonics firm Alpine Optoelectronics that year, and its shares surged on Nvidia-driven demand in 2024-25.
notes: Highly relevant to a data-center podcast because of Eoptolink, but Hu has a very low profile and left the board in 2020 (board history: http://vip.stock.finance.sina.com.cn/corp/go.php/vCI_CorpManager/stockid/300502.phtml). Chairman Gao Guangrong is the company's public face. Web-search budget ran out during this lane.

name: Guo Huaqiang
current_role: Founder and Director, Sunyard Technology (信雅达, SSE: 600571), Hangzhou
profile: Guo Huaqiang (郭华强, b. 1956) founded Hangzhou-based Sunyard Technology in 1996. Sunyard makes software and systems for banks and financial institutions. He was chairman until December 2017 and remains on the board for the 2025-2028 term, holding about 10.4m shares.
interesting_fact: He built Sunyard on banking know-how: the company he founded in 1996 makes banking software, an industry he knew from the inside.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Sunyard he was head of the software section in the technology department of ICBC's Zhejiang branch, then vice-chairman and president of Hangzhou Xinli Electronics. He studied finance at China Central Radio & TV University (1986) and did graduate business-management study at Zhejiang University.
notes: Low media profile. Current Sunyard chairman is Geng Junling, so the company board-secretary route (Ye Hui, per SSE filings) is the published channel. No public email found; the website is mostly script-rendered. Web-search budget ran out during this lane.

name: You Jianyi
current_role: Former chairman and general manager of Ningbo Tianpu Rubber Technology (天普股份, SSE: 605255), 2018 to Dec 2025; still a shareholder (9m shares as of 2026)
profile: You Jianyi (尤建义, b. 1963) built Ningbo Tianpu, which makes rubber hoses and parts for the auto industry, and took it public in Shanghai in 2020. He chaired the company until December 2025. After a 2025 share transfer, a new board took over in January 2026 chaired by Yang Gongyifan.
interesting_fact: In 2025-26 he handed control of his listed auto-parts company to a new owner group. Since January 2026 the board has been chaired by Yang Gongyifan, who was reportedly behind the deal.
deep_cut_fact: Before Tianpu he was general manager of Ninghai Sitong Testing Instrument Co. and then chairman and GM of Ningbo Tianpu Auto Parts. He holds the professional title of senior economist (高级经济师).
notes: Possible data-center/AI angle: the new Tianpu chairman Yang Gongyifan is reportedly the founder of AI-chip (TPU) startup Zhonghao Xinying, which explains the 2025 control-transfer story; this was not verified here because the search budget ran out.
